events.title: Nestorius becomes Archbishop of Constantinople
events.description: Nestorius was consecrated archbishop of the eastern capital. His teaching on the two natures of Christ was condemned at Ephesus in 431, and the Church of the East that kept his name spread as far as China.
events.html: Nestorius was consecrated archbishop of the eastern capital. His teaching on the two natures of Christ was condemned at Ephesus in 431, and the Church of the East that kept his name spread as far as China.

events.title: James I charters the Virginia Company
events.description: King James I granted a charter to the Virginia Company's London and Plymouth branches to settle the North American coast. The London company founded Jamestown the following year.
events.html: King James I granted a charter to the Virginia Company's London and Plymouth branches to settle the North American coast. The London company founded Jamestown the following year.

events.title: Statute of Anne, the first copyright law, takes effect
events.description: Britain's Statute of Anne came into force, vesting copyright in authors rather than printers for a term of 14 years, renewable once. It set the principle on which modern copyright law is built.
events.html: Britain's Statute of Anne came into force, vesting copyright in authors rather than printers for a term of 14 years, renewable once. It set the principle on which modern copyright law is built.

events.title: Mount Tambora reaches its cataclysmic climax
events.description: The Indonesian volcano produced the largest eruption in recorded history, killing tens of thousands on Sumbawa and Lombok. Its ash cooled the globe, making 1816 the 'Year Without a Summer'.
events.html: The Indonesian volcano produced the largest eruption in recorded history, killing tens of thousands on Sumbawa and Lombok. Its ash cooled the globe, making 1816 the 'Year Without a Summer'.

events.title: Titanic leaves Southampton on her maiden voyage
events.description: RMS Titanic, the largest ship afloat, sailed from Southampton for New York via Cherbourg and Queenstown. Five days later she struck an iceberg and sank with the loss of more than 1,500 lives.
events.html: RMS Titanic, the largest ship afloat, sailed from Southampton for New York via Cherbourg and Queenstown. Five days later she struck an iceberg and sank with the loss of more than 1,500 lives.

events.title: Good Friday Agreement is signed in Belfast
events.description: The British and Irish governments and most Northern Ireland parties agreed a settlement creating a power-sharing assembly and cross-border bodies. It largely brought three decades of the Troubles to a close.
